add.unverified: Google warns that the app is unverified the first time. Spending only reads card alert emails and never changes your mail.
import.title: Import a statement

import.chooseCardHint: Choose the card this file is for.
settings.title: Settings
settings.sample: These are the sample household’s settings. Changes last until the page reloads.
settings.budgetHint: What the household means to spend on its cards each month. Leave it empty to compare with last month instead.
settings.currencyHint: The household’s currency, in every Huishouden app.
settings.neverCountHint: Charges whose description has one of these words don't count as spending: rent, the mortgage, paying off a card.
card.alertWordsHint: The address this card's purchase alerts come from, or words only those emails contain. Separate with commas.
cards.intro: The household's cards. Statement files and card alert emails are matched to a card by its last 4 digits, so every member's imports name a card the same way.
rules.intro: New charges get the category of the longest phrase their description contains. Your own phrases win over the starting ones when they are more specific.
email.title: Card alert emails
email.intro: Spending searches the connected inboxes for each card's alert words and these Gmail labels.
sheet.title: Bring settings from a Google Sheet
sheet.intro: For households that used the Sheet and its script: brings the Cards, Categories and Alert labels tabs in once. The Sheet is only read.
sheet.cardsTab: Cards tab (Last4, Card, Alert source, Alert keywords)
sheet.rules: {n, plural, one {# category rule} other {# category rules}}
sheet.doneHint: Add each card's alert address under Cards so Check email finds its alerts.
sheet.notFound: No Sheet at that link, or this account cannot open it.
email.nothingToSearch: Add the words your card alerts contain (the sender’s address, say) to a card in Settings first.
inbox.title: Alert inbox
inbox.intro: Card alerts can go to any Gmail account, not only the one you sign in with. Connect the account your alerts arrive at, and Spending checks it every few minutes, even when nobody has the app open.
inbox.found: {n, plural, one {# purchase found {ago}} other {# purchases found {ago}}}
inbox.error.revoked: Google access was removed. Reconnect to keep checking.
inbox.error.notMember: Whoever connected it can no longer see Spending. Connect it again.
inbox.error.signedOut: Whoever connected it signed out everywhere. Connect it again.
inbox.error.nothingToSearch: Nothing to search for: add the address each card’s alerts come from (Cards), or Gmail labels below.
inbox.error.gmail: Gmail didn’t answer the last check. It tries again on its own.
inbox.error.firestore: The last check’s purchases couldn’t be saved. It tries again on its own.
inbox.privacy: Spending asks Google for read-only access to the inbox you choose. It only searches for your cards’ alert words and these labels, and keeps only what it writes for each purchase: date, shop, amount, category and card. Disconnect removes the access at Google and deletes what was kept for it.
inbox.unverified: Gmail access is a restricted permission. Until Google has reviewed the app, Google shows a warning that it is unverified, and at most 100 Google accounts can connect.
inbox.unavailable: Alert inboxes aren’t set up on this server.
inbox.err.denied: Google didn’t allow reading that inbox. In Google’s window, tick the box to view your email messages.
inbox.err.notAllowed: Only admins and members can manage alert inboxes, and only an admin or whoever connected an inbox can disconnect it.
inbox.err.quota: The household’s daily limit is used up. Try again tomorrow.
inbox.err.unavailable: Alert inboxes aren’t available right now.
inbox.err.network: Couldn’t reach the alert checker. Check the connection and try again.
glance.inboxStopped: {address} needs reconnecting: Google access was removed.
add.connectInboxText: Choose the Gmail account your card alerts arrive at.

inbox.review: {n, plural, one {Couldn’t read # email — check it} other {Couldn’t read # emails — check them}}
inbox.undoConfirm: {n, plural, one {Remove the # purchase it added?} other {Remove the # purchases it added?}}
inbox.err.notLastImport: That import isn’t the last one any more. Look again and try once more.
review.title: Emails to check
review.intro: These emails looked like purchases, but Spending couldn’t tell the shop or the amount for sure, so it added nothing for them. Only you see them: they’re your email.
